facts.raw_span: dual-chamber pacemaker implantation in the left prepectoral area
an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site
antibiotics (amoxicillin–clavulanate, 1 g three times daily) were started empirically
A swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis
the lesion had darkened and enlarged

concepts.why: The patient presented with fever and an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site, and a swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis.
The patient developed an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site, and was treated with antibiotics.
A swab of the lesion grew Staphylococcus epidermidis.
The patient developed an infection related to the pacemaker implantation.
The patient presented with fever, elevated inflammatory syndrome, and was treated with antibiotics.
The patient developed an infection related to the pacemaker implantation, with a lesion over the implant site.

rationales.F03: Pacemaker implantation is a known risk factor for pocket infection.
rationales.F06: The presence of an inflamed, infiltrating, necrotic lesion over the implant site is highly suggestive of infection.
rationales.F10: The growth of Staphylococcus epidermidis from a swab of the lesion is diagnostic of infection.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including fever and an inflamed lesion over the implant site, along with the growth of Staphylococcus epidermidis from the lesion swab, specifically point to an infection at the pacemaker implant site, making Pacemaker pocket infection the most fitting diagnosis.
